equivalent.M2: The result is 0 when start is after end. The only way to reach the replaced constant is the guard's own return value, and the faulty version returns 1 there. So it is not equivalent: a test with start after end must expect exactly 0, not 1.
equivalent.M16: Behaviour differs only in the type: a float vs integer division. A total of whole minutes is equal either way in value, so only a type check on the result (integer) can tell them apart. Test that the result is an integer.
equivalent.M21: The first search window is widened to larger windows when nothing is found, so one more day in its length changes the result only if an open lies exactly at the edge, which the wider fallback windows cover anyway. No input gives a different answer.
equivalent.M22: The second window is only used when the first has no open, and then it is one day longer. An open falling exactly on that extra day would be found by the third window anyway, with the same value, so the outcome is identical.
equivalent.M23: The last window is one day longer, and only changes whether an error is raised for an open exactly ten years out. This is not realistically testable on real calendars.
equivalent.M5: A calendar defines break_start and break_end together or not at all. So 'both present' and 'either present' give the same answer for every real calendar.
equivalent.M8: The lower bound is only reached for zero or negative lengths, and the change makes it 1 nanosecond instead of 0. The total is floored to whole minutes, so no input changes the result.
equivalent.M9: When the break start equals the session open, the replacement value is that same open. The result is identical either way.
equivalent.M10: When the break end equals the session close, the replacement value is that same close. The result is identical either way.
equivalent.M17: The Timedelta floor division already returns a plain integer, so wrapping it in int() changes neither the value nor the type.
equivalent.M19: The search only starts a few days earlier or later than needed and then keeps opens after the timestamp. A one-day change in the lookback gives the same first open.
